In the face of huge increases in revenue between 1974 and 1975, the Crow Tribal Council has chosen to disburse much of the increase in the form of per capita payments (more than $800,000 in fiscal year 1976). This action removes opportunities to invest for future revenue gains, but does attempt to deal with immediate income insufficiencies on the reservation.
There is currently, however, an attempt to alter this situation by investing some of the new coal revenues. Although 60 percent of coal royalty revenues will be disbursed to tribal members on a per capita basis, the Crow Tribe plans to use 20 percent of the revenue for land purchases. A portion of the remaining 20 percent will be deposited in banks for tribal needs as deemed necessary by the Tribal Council and the Bureau of Indian Affairs. Per capita payments involve 5,780 persons who are on the tribal rolls. Each of these individuals is to receive $145 per year (Memorandum to Patrick Stands Over Bull, July 24, 1975; Crow Tribal Resolution No. 76-02).
To summarize, tribal expenditures are largely given to maintenance of the tribal government, to the provision of limited community services and to the administration of loans. The only investment of funds for revenue-providing enterprises is for the tribally-owned Sun Lodge and the placement of funds in banks and U.S. Treasury notes. All of these are rather limited in total amounts invested and in investment returns. Interest payments on funds in the U.S. Treasury and in commercial banks amounted to $80,715 in fiscal year 1974 (Crow Tribal Budget Status, 1974).
